interactions.summary: Jiang uses Paul's line to argue that some realities, especially God and consciousness, can never be proven by scientific measurement and therefore must be assumed in faith if one wants to reason toward truth at all.

Students push Jiang's attack on scientific stagnation by citing particle accelerators and challenging his authority to judge physics, while Jiang doubles down that quantum mechanics was the last truly major breakthrough and demands homework instead of immediate concession.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Student challenge, student rebuke, and Jiang answer

speaker_notes.note: This turn is argumentative rather than inquisitive: the speaker rebukes Jiang's competence to assess scientific breakthroughs and tells him to consult scientists directly.

claims.claim: Jiang says realities such as God, consciousness, and human connection to God cannot be proven by measurement yet still must be assumed through faith if the world is to make sense.
Jiang argues that contemporary science has run into a dead end, naming physics and neuroscience as examples of disciplines that no longer reach the deepest questions.
A student offers the particle accelerator as evidence that physics has still produced meaningful insight into matter even if that does not settle Jiang's larger complaint.
Another student objects that Jiang is relying on articles and is not qualified to declare what counts as a breakthrough in science.
Jiang responds that quantum mechanics was the last major breakthrough in physics and that later programs such as string theory do not count as breakthroughs on that level.

The exchange makes burden of proof itself part of the classroom dispute: the students demand evidence for Jiang's civilizational critique while Jiang treats the physics question as homework that should confirm his view.

signature_moments.moment: Faith is recast as the precondition for reasoning whenever the most important realities cannot be measured into existence.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you have to assume certain things about the world through your faith
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's clearest epistemic formula and bridges the Dante discussion to Jiang's anti-scientistic critique.

signature_moments.moment: Physics and neuroscience are named as dead ends rather than triumphant frontiers.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you look at physics you look at neuroscience it's all a dead end
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's sharpest provocation against modern scientific self-confidence in the packet.

signature_moments.moment: The science dispute gets compressed into a dare: name the last genuinely new theory in physics.
signature_moments.source_phrase: tell me in the past 70 years what major theory in physics have we had
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It shows how Jiang turns a metaphysical discussion into a challenge to the prestige of scientific progress.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's usage for the unseen premises, such as God or consciousness, that must be trusted before reasoning can unfold.
Jiang's characterization of scientific paradigms that keep generating technical work without resolving the deepest metaphysical questions.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-06-17 Jiang tightens the packet's ontology of faith into a historical complaint about modern science: the unseen must be assumed in faith because contemporary physics and neuroscience have stalled at the deepest level.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang's summary of the last major breakthrough in physics is a classroom claim rather than a source-grounded historical finding, so it should be preserved as his polemical position rather than normalized as fact.
